_comment: SYNTHETIC, and deliberately so -- the one exception this repo already
makes, for the same reason. A real `/portfolio/balance` payload is
operator data: it is Joe's account balance, and his standing ruling is
that account and fills data never enter this public repo, even
sanitized. So this follows the precedent ADR 0035 sets: a synthetic
payload plus a SHAPE assertion, with the inconsistency recorded as the
decision rather than left as a bug to fix. (That ADR is about a
different third party, and its name is deliberately not written here:
the guard in tests/test_captures_carry_their_request.py greps fixture
TEXT, not fixture payloads, so citing it by name in prose trips it.)
The shape below is not invented. It was read off 72 real captured
payloads held OUTSIDE the repo under `data/` (gitignored), which
returned exactly one shape with no variation:
- top-level `balance` is an INTEGER, and it is CENTS
- each `balance_breakdown[].balance` is a STRING matching \d+\.\d{4},
and it is DOLLARS
Those two readings agree with each other to within 0.0065 dollars across
all 72; under any other pairing they disagree by a factor of ~100.
`docs/measurements/2026-09-18-the-shard-balance-is-dollars.md`.
The figures here are round numbers chosen to make the unit test
arithmetic legible, and the cross-check holds on them too:
(the 0.01 discrepancy is the same kind the real captures show).
